title: I Took the Tile-Saw Reservation to the Mentor Who Left My Blade Wet

parts.text: I stepped to saw one at 2:09 p.m. and mentor Gita was already cutting on my numbered tray. The board said: ONE SAW. SIXTY MINUTES. BLADE DRAIN WITH THE BOOKING. I was thirty-eight, shop member, holding a tile ticket that listed our lot. Gita shrugged. "Mentors are the wet." I photographed the board, the booking, and her slurry on my pan. Then I asked for the saw log. At 2:17 the shop pinged why Gita's name was on my blade. I kept my voice shop-quiet and let the timestamp talk. A board is only a board until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The shop can see Gita's slurry on my pan during our booking.

social.video_title: She cut on my numbered tray and left the blade wet — Part 1/2
social.description: Tile saw, a mentor on my pan, a sixty-minute board she posted. I logged the slurry. Would you have asked for the saw log?

parts.text: Gita called it a splash until the shop asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the slurry still. The blade went back to my drain. Gita ran her own sixty and told the next mentor atmosphere was always about score. Score is a word mentors use when a booking exists. Saw policy now has a second line: MENTORS ARE NOT THE WET. I keep our tray on a labeled rack. Gita brown-bags her jokes. The shop finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Mentors are not the wet — Part 2/2
social.description: Saw log, numbered tray, and a second line on the board. Was a splash ever my pan?
